title: Minimal Recovery Theorem orientation and universalizable evidence-sufficiency imperative

artificial_cognitive_actor.identity_and_observation_limits: Tool and model family information is runtime-supplied. No claim is made about hidden implementation internals, legal personhood, independent intent, or authorship rights.

human_contributions.description: Provided the Minimal Recovery Theorem formulation, its recovery-relevant equivalence, observation-fiber criterion, fail-closed rule, witness interpretation, delayed-choice epistemic boundary, finite-model scope, and condensed conclusion.
Directed persistence in the canonical QIK-VRT repository as an orientation guide and as a translatable cross-domain guideline in the sense of the categorical imperative.

artificial_cognitive_contributions.description: Bound Authority main and reobserved that the existing delayed-choice hardware-witness tranche already contains the theorem, its formal note, Lean source reference, finite-model scope, and fail-closed boundaries; avoided duplicating that established source.

Extended the existing German orientation with explicit delayed-choice and finite-model boundaries, drafted the additive cross-domain evidence-sufficiency imperative, and linked both through the existing tranche README.

Specified that the cross-domain rule does not define domain-correct actions, establish Kantian ethics, legal compliance, medical correctness, scientific truth, or authorize an external effect; added a focused static regression test.
